solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post, which drops the counts, so each count is read off the blogger's answer

clue.text: Insect with wings clipped crawled around

indicators.note: a bird with clipped wings has lost its extremities, so the word loses its outer letters
turned around, the trimmed word is read from its far end back

blocks.note: to drag oneself along is to crawl slowly

explanation.surface: A bug with damaged wings could only creep about.
explanation.walkthrough: DRAGGED loses both D's to leave RAGGE, which turned round gives EGGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The eggar is a large moth, so an insect; the name comes from its egg-shaped cocoon.

clue.text: Leaks what Cockney 'umorist does in audition

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the phrase is to be judged by its sound

blocks.note: a Cockney drops the H, so a humorist who jests becomes 'e jests

explanation.surface: A Cockney comic lets slip secrets while trying out for a part.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'umorist is the hint that the H is dropped throughout, as in Cockney speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To egest is to discharge or excrete from the body, so it fits leaks as a verb.

clue.text: Fish from historic Scottish bar close to Dundee

indicators.note: what is closest to the end of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: an old Scots word for a bar or rod of metal
the last letter of Dundee

explanation.surface: Fish served in an old Scottish pub near Dundee.
explanation.definitionFit: A gade is a fish of the cod family, a name found in older dictionaries.

clue.text: Stone taken off instead of getting over

indicators.note: something taken off is removed, so those letters come out of the longer word

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for the stone, a British weight of 14 pounds
as in a deposit set against a loan, in exchange for

explanation.surface: Losing weight in place of getting over something.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove ST from AGAINST. A stone is a British unit of body weight, 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Over, as in 'do it over', means once more, the same as again.

clue.text: Boisterous locally, two score runs for side in Fremantle

indicators.note: one thing standing for another means it takes the other's place in the word
the side of a word is its edge, here the opening letter of the place named

blocks.note: a score is twenty, so two of them make forty
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
the first letter of Fremantle, the letter swapped out

explanation.surface: A rowdy Australian cricket side piles up forty runs in Fremantle.
explanation.walkthrough: In FORTY, R takes the place of F, the side letter of Fremantle. Fremantle is the port city of Perth, so 'locally' and the setting point to Australian slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Rorty is Australian and British slang for rowdy, lively or boisterous.

clue.text: Chinese copier used in Chancery department once

blocks.note: the Han are the majority Chinese people
one who apes, an imitator

explanation.surface: A Chinese photocopier installed in a legal office.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hanaper was an old office of the English Court of Chancery that collected fees, named from the hamper holding the writs.

clue.text: Brazilian book out trashes dyeing matter

indicators.note: out means removed, so that letter is dropped from the word beside it
to trash something is to wreck it, leaving the letters in disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A Brazilian reader, finding the book gone, wrecks the dyeing equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Alizarin is the red colouring substance from madder root, used in dyeing.

clue.text: Chief officer overseeing police station not available for releasing lady

indicators.note: a station releasing someone lets them go, so those letters leave the word

blocks.note: an aga is a Turkish commander or chief officer
a thana is a police station in India
N/A, the abbreviation for not available

explanation.surface: The chief officer at the station is unavailable to let a woman out of custody.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'overseeing' means sitting above, so the chief officer comes first. N/A is the usual shorthand for not available; a thana is an Indian police station.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha is a woman's name, and Mephisto conventionally lets a lady clue a female forename.

clue.text: Criticise rating on child right away showing all is in flux (9, two words)

indicators.note: with the right gone away, the abbreviation for right drops out of the word

blocks.note: to pan a show is to criticise it
a rating is an ordinary sailor, as is a tar
a child is an heir to its parents
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A critic slates a child's score at once, proving everything keeps changing.
explanation.walkthrough: HEIR loses R to give HEI.
explanation.definitionFit: Panta rhei, Greek for 'everything flows', is the saying attributed to Heraclitus that all is in constant change.

clue.text: Smart youths take lingerie leaving note

indicators.note: the letter leaving the word departs from it, so it is cut out

blocks.note: R, from Latin recipe, is the abbreviation for take on prescriptions
undies is a casual word for underwear
N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: Sharp young men help themselves to underwear and leave a note.
explanation.walkthrough: UNDIES without N leaves UDIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudies, short for rude boys, were sharply dressed Jamaican youths of the 1960s ska scene.

clue.text: Outburst about awfully gory and bizarre ornament

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, leaving those letters in disorder
about means surrounding, so the outer word wraps around the rest

blocks.note: a gale of laughter is an outburst
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: An outburst over a horribly bloody and weird decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: A gargoyle is a grotesque carved figure on a building, often a waterspout, hence a bizarre ornament.

clue.text: Madrigal composer number one approves current cast

indicators.note: cast in the sense of cast off or thrown away, so that letter is discarded

blocks.note: number one is a childish euphemism for a wee
to like something is to approve of it
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: The top composer of madrigals endorses the present performers.
explanation.walkthrough: LIKES loses I to give LKES.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Weelkes was an English composer of madrigals around 1600.

clue.text: Study a spot in retreat behind pub with projecting gallery

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the words are read from end to start
behind places the first part after the other, so the order is fixed

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
a den is a private study
taken as written
a zit is a pimple

explanation.surface: A study with a stain withdrawn behind a pub that has a balcony.
explanation.definitionFit: A bartizan is an overhanging turret or gallery on a castle wall, so bartizaned means fitted with one.

clue.text: Issue in volume put into eastern language

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

blocks.note: volume is size or bulk
to issue is to emit

explanation.surface: A book's printing is translated into an oriental tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: To semitize is to make Semitic, for instance rendering into Hebrew or Arabic, languages of the Near East.

clue.text: Dull area rather for underground store

blocks.note: a matt finish is dull, not glossy
A is the abbreviation for area
as in more or rather, sooner

explanation.surface: A dull region would be better as an underground storeroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattamore is a subterranean chamber or granary, from the Arabic for a storage pit.

clue.text: Lady's loose gown unsettling to boyfriend

indicators.note: read as un-settling: something unseated is removed from its place

blocks.note: a manto is a woman's loose robe, a variant of manteau
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman's flowing dress proves disturbing to her boyfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: Man is an informal word for a husband or lover, as in 'her man'.

clue.text: No end of worship in excited press after Captain raised lots of money

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means lifted up, so the word reads from bottom to top
the closing letter of worship is to be taken out of the word that follows
excited means agitated, so the letters are stirred up
after places the rearranged press second, behind the captain's name

blocks.note: Captain Tom Moore, who raised millions for charity walking laps of his garden
taken as written

explanation.surface: The excited press reports how Captain Tom raised a fortune with a wholly secular act of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: PRESS loses P, the end of worship, and the rest is rearranged; MOT comes first. Captain Tom was the British veteran whose 2020 fundraising walk raised over £30 million.
explanation.definitionFit: Motser is Australian slang for a large sum of money, especially a gambling win.

clue.text: Region consumes one timeless refreshment, a frothy dessert

indicators.note: without time means the abbreviation for time is dropped from the next word
consuming something takes it inside, so the outer word swallows the rest

blocks.note: a zone is a region
a means one
bait is an old word for a refreshment or snack on a journey

explanation.surface: A district eats up a single refreshment that never ends: a fluffy pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Bait as a snack is old or dialect usage, from the meal given to travellers and their horses at an inn.
explanation.definitionFit: Zabaione is the Italian dessert of egg yolks, sugar and Marsala whisked until frothy.

clue.text: Thrash for one with large appetite

blocks.note: first meaning: a dialect verb, to beat or flog
second meaning: the huge sea mammal, as in eating like one

explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like a punishment for a glutton; the two halves are separate senses of one five-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb meaning to lash or beat shares its spelling with the sea giant proverbially associated with enormous eating.

clue.text: Footless fools seen in boozers

indicators.note: without a foot means the abbreviation for foot is removed from the word for fools

blocks.note: a soft is a simpleton or fool

explanation.surface: Legless idiots are a common sight in pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: SOFTS loses F for foot. Footless is also slang for very drunk, so the whole clue describes the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: Sots are habitual drunkards, the sort found in pubs; sot once also meant fool.

clue.text: Room on boat in choppy sea for reserves

indicators.note: choppy water is rough and broken up, so these letters are tossed about
in places the first group inside the second

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging
RM is the abbreviation for room
Noah's ark was a boat

explanation.surface: Space aboard a vessel on rough water is kept back for those held in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark is to set aside for a purpose, the same as to reserve; both are verbs here.

clue.text: Oxidised element in battery one changed

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A battery with one rusted part inside it has been replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Ytterbia is ytterbium oxide, so it is an element in oxidised form.

clue.text: Reversing forgotten award and benefit heads off clash

indicators.note: with their heads off, both words lose their opening letters
reversing means going backwards, so the combined letters read from the end

blocks.note: arett is an obsolete Spenserian verb meaning to award or allot
pay is a benefit received for work

explanation.surface: Backing a lost prize and its benefits, leaders head off a conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: ARETT and PAY lose their first letters to give RETT and AY, and the whole is then read backwards. 'Forgotten' warns that the award word is long obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Clash is a Scots word for gossip or idle talk, and yatter is Scots for incessant chatter.

clue.text: No date in family upset the last in line (6, two words)

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word reads from bottom to top
in places one item inside the other

blocks.note: a family name, as in the honour of the name
n.d. is the bibliographic abbreviation for no date

explanation.surface: A family is upset over an undated item.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns the word upside down, which reads it backwards; n.d. is the standard bibliographic note for an undated work.
explanation.definitionFit: An end man is the person at the end of a row, originally of a minstrel-show line.

clue.text: Lacking focus, newspaper closed years ago

indicators.note: the focus of a word is its centre, so the middle letter goes

blocks.note: a sheet is slang for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A paper with no clear direction folded long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: SHEET loses its central E.
explanation.definitionFit: Shet is an obsolete form of shut, so means closed in old usage.

clue.text: Stimulant from introduction of tonic put before German poet

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter of tonic
Heinrich Heine, nineteenth-century German poet

explanation.surface: A pick-me-up drink is offered to a German poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Theine is caffeine as found in tea, a stimulant.

clue.text: Could be represented as one term in yoga

blocks.note: taken as written
one rendered as the indefinite article followed by the letter that stands for one

explanation.surface: Something that might be shown as a single word in yoga.
explanation.walkthrough: As one becomes 'as an A', the letter A being the usual stand-in for one.
explanation.definitionFit: An asana is any posture in yoga, the Sanskrit word for a seated pose.

clue.text: Old-fashioned manner, Tom's foremost indeed in celebrity book put out

indicators.note: foremost means at the front, so only the leading letter is kept
put out means ejected, so that letter is expelled from the word
in places the pair inside the shortened word

blocks.note: sleb is slang for a celebrity
B is the abbreviation for book
the first letter of Tom
I is an old spelling of ay or aye, meaning yes indeed

explanation.surface: An old-world manner, chiefly Tom's, really shows in a celebrity book being published.
explanation.walkthrough: SLEB without B leaves SLE, and T plus I go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stile is an archaic spelling of style, meaning a manner of doing things.

clue.text: Men in board game out of bounds

indicators.note: the bounds of a word are its edges, and these are put out of it

blocks.note: chess is played on a board

explanation.surface: Pieces in a board game have strayed off the board.
explanation.walkthrough: CHESS loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A he is a male, so hes are men or males, the plural of the pronoun used as a noun.

clue.text: Strict Jew carries a passport, for instance

blocks.note: to carry something is to have it
a passport is an example of identification, ID

explanation.surface: An orthodox Jew carries his travel documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hasid is a member of a strictly orthodox Jewish sect founded in eighteenth-century Poland.

clue.text: Asphalt processed in quantities without cover

indicators.note: with its covers off, a word loses its outermost letters at each end
processed means worked over, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tarmac is treated in bulk loads without a top layer.
explanation.definitionFit: Uintaite, or gilsonite, is a natural black asphalt found in Utah's Uinta basin.

clue.text: Time in Scotland of last waltz?

indicators.note: of means taken from, so the letters are drawn out of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: When the final dance happens north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: Twal is Scots for twelve, so an hour, a time; the question mark admits the cheeky definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Twal is the Scots form of twelve, as in twal o'clock, so a time of day there.

clue.text: One of the military brass, amazing Sir Tom enthrals Britain on reaching a ton

indicators.note: amazing is read as astonishing or confusing, so the letters are thrown into a new order
to enthral is to hold captive, so the jumble keeps the next letters inside
reaching means arriving at, so the last piece is added on the end

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging
B is the abbreviation for Britain
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for ton

explanation.surface: A knighted Tom thrills the nation by scoring a century.
explanation.walkthrough: Military brass suggests top officers; it means a brass player in a military band.
explanation.definitionFit: A trombonist plays the trombone, a brass instrument, as found in military bands.

clue.text: John Laing surprisingly coming first to supply a church member

indicators.note: surprisingly hints at an unexpected arrangement of these letters
coming first fixes the order: the rearranged name goes in front

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging
john and can are both American slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: The John Laing building firm surprisingly provides for a churchgoer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John Laing' reads as a single name; John is separate and means the lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: An Anglican belongs to the Church of England or a church in communion with it.

clue.text: Record again with one feeling regret piano's missing

indicators.note: missing means absent, so that letter is left out of the word

blocks.note: someone who repents feels regret
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Recording a second take, the remorseful player finds the piano gone.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-enter data is to record it a second time in a ledger or system.

clue.text: No small seat for Roman magistrate

indicators.note: no means without, so the next letter is left off

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a sedile is a stone seat for clergy beside a church altar

explanation.surface: No little chair was provided for the Roman official.
explanation.definitionFit: An edile, or aedile, was a Roman official responsible for public buildings, games and markets.
